lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: By Pluto, Aeacus, give me the full tour. Everything in Hades.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Everything is not easy, Menippus. But the main features, certainly. That there is Cerberus — you know him. And this ferryman here is the one who brought you across. You saw the lake and the Pyriphlegethon on the way in.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I know all that. I know you, too — gate duty. I’ve seen the King and the Furies. Show me the old human stock. Especially the famous ones.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: This is Agamemnon. This is Achilles. Beside him, Idomeneus. This is Odysseus. Then Ajax and Diomedes, and the rest of the Greek first team.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well, Homer. Look at the leading characters from your recitations, dumped on the floor — unrecognisable, shapeless. Dust, all of it, and a great deal of nonsense. ‘Feeble heads,’ indeed. And this one, Aeacus — who is he?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Cyrus. This is Croesus. Above him, Sardanapalus. Above them, Midas. And that one is Xerxes.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So that is the trash Greece used to shudder at — the man who bridged the Hellespont and wanted to sail through mountains. And look at Croesus. Aeacus, let me slap Sardanapalus across the face.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Absolutely not. You’ll smash his skull. It’s a delicate, womanish thing.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then I’ll spit on him, at least. Fair enough for a man-woman.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Would you like me to show you the wise men too?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: God, yes.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: First, here is Pythagoras.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Greetings, Euphorbus. Or Apollo. Or whatever you’re going by now.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: And to you, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Is your thigh not gold anymore?

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: No. But let me see whether that bag of yours has anything edible in it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Beans, my good man. So not edible for you.

lines.speaker: Pythagoras
lines.text: Just give them here. The doctrines are different among the dead. I’ve learned that beans and the heads of one’s parents are not at all the same thing down here.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: This is Solon, son of Execestides; that there is Thales; beside them Pittacus and the others. Seven in all, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: These are the only ones here without grief, Aeacus. Bright-faced, unlike the rest. But that one there, full of ash like a loaf baked under the coals, all blistered up — who is that?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Empedocles, Menippus. Arrived half-cooked from Etna.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Best of bronze-footed men, what happened? Why did you throw yourself into the crater?

lines.speaker: Empedocles
lines.text: A kind of melancholy, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, by Zeus. Vanity, pretension, and a very heavy cold in the head — that’s what charred you, sandals and all. Not that you didn’t deserve it. Still, the trick did you no good. You were caught dead. And Socrates, Aeacus — where is he, exactly?

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Most of the time he talks nonsense with Nestor and Palamedes over there.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All the same, I’d like to see him, if he’s here.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: Do you see the bald one?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: They’re all bald. That would identify every single one of them.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: I mean the snub-nosed one.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Same problem. They’re all snub-nosed.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Are you looking for me, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Very much, Socrates.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: How are things in Athens?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Many of the young men say they’re philosophers. If you saw the outfits and the walk, you’d say: first-rate philosophers.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: I’ve seen a great many of them.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then you’ve seen what sort came down here to join you: Aristippus, and Plato himself — one reeking of perfume, the other having mastered the art of waiting on Sicilian tyrants.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: And what do they think of me?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: In that respect, Socrates, you are a fortunate man. Everyone thinks you were marvellous, and that you knew everything — when, since one ought to tell the truth, I suppose, you knew nothing.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: I told them that myself. They thought it was irony.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And who are these around you?

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: Charmides, Menippus. Phaedrus. And the son of Clinias.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent, Socrates. You’re still practising your craft down here. Not neglecting the beautiful boys.

lines.speaker: Socrates
lines.text: What else could I do that would be pleasanter? Come lie down near us, if you like.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, by Zeus. I’m off to live next door to Croesus and Sardanapalus. I expect to get a good deal of laughing done listening to them howl.

lines.speaker: Aeacus
lines.text: And I must go too, before some dead man slips past us and escapes. You’ll see the rest another time, Menippus.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Go on. This is enough for now, Aeacus.
